name: estate-clocks
summary: Chronos: did every declared clock actually deliver, inside its own tolerance? bin/estate-clocks renders the DECLARED cadence; this legion measures the DELIVERED one, so a clock that stopped firing is a finding rather than a silence
_comment: WHAT THIS FILE IS. Each entry under `obligations` is one clock the estate
declares it runs. Nothing here schedules anything: Chronos reads the
workflow's own recorded runs and compares OBSERVED delivery against the
obligation's own tolerance. The scheduler and the executor keep the
monopoly on running work (AGENTS.md section 6); this legion only answers
'did it actually run?' and reports.
WHY TOLERANCE IS NOT THE NOMINAL CADENCE. idp#5918 measured GitHub cron
delivering 20-70x later than declared. Measured again 2026-11-08 against
origin/main, scheduled runs only: ping declares every 5 min and its
observed gaps are 190-400 min; estate-state declares every 15 min and
delivers 192-499 min. Setting tolerance to the cron expression would
redden the gate permanently on day one, and a gate that is always red is
ignored. Tolerance is the age at which a MISSING RUN is news: set above
measured reality, and tightenable as the time base improves.
max_age_minutes semantics: MISSED_CYCLE when the newest SCHEDULED run is
older than this. state=retired entries are never graded -- a retired clock
is silent on purpose, which is a different fact from a dead one.
MEASUREMENTS BELOW ARE FROM 2026-11-08 AND CARRY THEIR EVIDENCE. Where a
number here ever disagrees with the live board, the live board is right and
this stanza is the thing to update -- that disagreement is itself a finding.

obligations.evidence: THE FOUNDER'S DELIVERY PATH. This is the one workflow that moves main. Measured 2026-11-08 over its last 100 runs: 1 schedule, 56 workflow_run, 43 workflow_dispatch. The single scheduled run was 2026-11-08T07:20:45Z. So the cron is not carrying the lane -- the event path is. That is worth knowing rather than assuming: if the event path ever stops, the */15 was never the net everyone believes it is.
obligations.catch_up: event-driven: workflow_run wakes it on CI completion

obligations.evidence: The dead-man's switch that tells the founder the estate is dark. If it cannot fire, no other silence in the estate can be trusted -- which is exactly why its own delivery has to be measured. Observed gaps 2026-11-08: 190-400 min against a declared 5.
Grades every critical lane against platform/ladder/critical-lanes.json from off the laptop. Observed gaps 2026-11-08: 172-427 min against a declared 30.
Publishes the estate's own state page. Observed gaps 2026-11-08: 192-499 min against a declared 15.

Weekly, and measured to deliver weekly: scheduled runs 2026-09-14, 09-21, 09-28, 10-05, 10-12, 10-19, 10-26, 11-02 -- eight consecutive Mondays. This is the control case: a clock whose declared cadence and delivered cadence agree, so the detector is proved not to cry wolf.

Measured 2026-11-08 over its last 100 runs: 99 push, 1 schedule (2026-11-03T10:50:30Z). A weekly clock with one scheduled fire visible. Graded rather than asserted -- if the run ages past tolerance the board says so.

RETIRED, and recorded as retired rather than as a ghost. GitHub reports this workflow state=deleted; it ran hourly and its last scheduled run was 2026-09-23T00:46:25Z. Retiring a clock is a decision, so it is baselined here on purpose instead of being allowlisted into silence. Set state back to active to revive it.

argon's own provenance guardians have not started since 2026-11-06 (metered minutes); this relay is the only thing checking argon main. Measured 2026-11-13 01:26Z: merged 22:45Z (PR #8023), zero scheduled runs in 2h40m, one manual dispatch (43326943278). A guard that does not run is consent; Chronos grades whether it ran.
Founder 2026-11-13: 'a schedule also for Chronos weekly'. Chronos grades its own weekly review: a silent week is a MISS.

obligations.declares_human: every 10 minutes (GitHub home; Cloudflare and mac homes knock by dispatch)
obligations.evidence: idp#8026: the pacemaker's own GitHub clock. Its other two homes are graded by the pacemaker itself (silent_homes).

coverage_floor_why: Chronos loop map (bin/idp-estate-clocks --coverage): the number of recurring declarations graded for delivery. It only rises; --coverage --gate refuses a tree below it. Measured 2026-11-13: 8 closed of 141 (chronos-weekly and estate-pacemaker added) declared.

pacemaker.why: ADR 0037 three homes, two providers. Each home knocks estate-pacemaker.yml with its name; every run tickets a home silent past its tolerance (minutes).
